title: Plan: Public API, docs, feature flags, benchmarks
description:
Final polish pass once all functionality is ported.

## Public API surface
- Clean `pub use` re-exports in lib.rs — users should only need `use swisseph::*` or `use swisseph::{Ephemeris, Body, Flags}`
- Builder pattern for Ephemeris:
  ```rust
  let eph = Ephemeris::builder()
      .ephe_path("./ephe")
      .sidereal(SiderealMode::Lahiri)
      .topo(lon, lat, alt)
      .build()?;
  ```
- Method naming: idiomatic Rust (snake_case, no `swe_` prefix), but consider a `compat` module with C-like names for users migrating

## Cargo feature flags
- `moshier` — always on (default feature), no file I/O
- `swisseph-files` — .se1 file backend
- `jpl` — JPL DE backend
- `serde` — Serialize/Deserialize for result types

## Documentation
- Doc comments on all public types, methods, enums
- Module-level docs explaining each domain
- README with: what it is, installation, quick example, feature flags, comparison to C version
- README/ledger preamble: state WHICH upstream C version the port is bit-compatible with (the golden oracle is pinned to the vendored `../swisseph` checkout; upstream v3 is in development and may fix quirks we deliberately replicate — see docs/swisseph-c-potential-bugs.md)
- Examples in `examples/` directory

## Benchmarks
- `criterion` benchmarks comparing Rust vs C for: calc() all planets, house computation, eclipse search
- Profile for hot spots (Chebyshev evaluation, nutation series, Moshier series)

## Testing
- Full integration test suite running all setest cases
- CI: test with each feature flag combination
- Numerical tolerance documentation

## FFI / Dart-isolates considerations (added 2026-07-01, Phase 12 planning)
The strategic consumer of this crate is a Dart binding (successor to swisseph.dart, which
binds the C lib and must copy the .so per isolate because of C's global state). The public
API design must not foreclose this. Requirements:

1. **`Ephemeris: Send + Sync`, pinned by a compile-time assertion test** — e.g.
   `fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() { }; assert_send_sync::<Ephemeris>();` in a unit
   test. This is the entire premise of the isolates story (one Rust-owned instance, raw
   opaque handle shared across every isolate, concurrent calc() with zero synchronization —
   vs. the C binding's copy-per-isolate). Mmap-backed SE1/JPL files are read-only after
   open so this should already hold; verify, don't assume. Any future feature that would
   add interior mutability to Ephemeris is an API-breaking decision, not an implementation
   detail.
2. **Plan the C-ABI flattening layer** — `Result`/enums/slices/`&str` don't cross FFI.
   Decide here (not improvise later): flutter_rust_bridge vs. hand-rolled cbindgen +
   `#[repr(C)]` mirror types + error-code + out-param convention. Whichever is chosen, the
   idiomatic Rust API stays primary and the FFI layer is a separate crate/module
   (`swisseph-ffi` or `ffi` feature) so cdylib build config doesn't pollute the lib crate.
3. **Ownership/handle model for Dart**: construction returns an opaque `*const Ephemeris`
   (Box::into_raw), isolates share the pointer value (Dart can send ints/pointers across
   isolates even though it can't send objects), destruction via an explicit free fn +
   Dart `NativeFinalizer`. Config is immutable after build — per-call overrides (the
   existing `calc_with_config` pattern) map cleanly to FFI params, which is exactly why the
   stateless design was chosen; keep that pattern rather than adding set_* mutators for
   FFI convenience.
4. **Capstone benchmark**: N isolates (or N Rust threads as a proxy) hammering `calc()` on
   one shared Ephemeris vs. the C-binding copy-per-isolate equivalent — the demo that
   proves the stateless design earned its keep. Belongs with the criterion suite.

## Dependencies
- All prior phases complete
decisions: No builder pattern for Ephemeris — the original description predates the finalized architecture invariant (construction via EphemerisConfig + Default). Rejected alternative: adding a builder anyway as sugar; rejected because it duplicates a config struct that is already Default-driven and would create a second construction path the FFI layer must mirror.

No compat module with C-style names. C-name discoverability handled by #[doc(alias = "swe_*")] on every Ephemeris method (rustdoc search finds them) + a README mapping table. Rejected alternative: a compat module re-exporting snake_case swe_* wrappers; rejected as permanent API surface bloat for a one-time migration convenience.

FFI approach decided: hand-rolled C ABI + cbindgen header in a future separate swisseph-ffi cdylib crate; opaque Box::into_raw handle, i32 error codes + out-params, no set_* mutators (per-call config overrides map to the existing *_with_config pattern). Rejected alternative: flutter_rust_bridge — the API is flat numeric data with no async/streams, the Dart consumer already speaks dart:ffi against the C ABI, and the isolate-shared raw-pointer handle model needs a hand-auditable ABI, not generated glue. Recorded durably in Polish 6/7 (docs/ffi-design.md).

Feature-flag layout: no 'moshier' feature — Moshier is unconditional code with zero deps; features gate the file backends (swisseph-files, jpl, both default-on so default builds keep the full golden suite), serde, and star-tools (making the bin-only clap/ureq deps optional). --no-default-features yields a bitflags-only, wasm-friendly build.

'Full integration suite running all setest cases' descoped: the golden differential batteries (thousands of cases across ~30 test files) already exceed setest's coverage for the ported surface; CI-per-feature-combo becomes tools/test-features.sh (no hosted CI assumed).
